key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while preserving electronic uniformity and suppressing aging-induced optoelectronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone is an insufficient quality metric for designing durable perovskite solar cells.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting in pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, largely retaining optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency or operational-lifetime results, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
